transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (AcornWave CTO), Daniel Ortiz (AcornWave Platform Eng), Li Wei (AcornWave Security Lead), Tom Alvarez (AcornWave Data Eng)
Recording ID: acw-20261113-94f2

Summary (auto):
AcornWave is evaluating Redwood for a mixed workload: customer-facing chat plus internal embeddings for search. They want to understand SDK integration (LangChain/LlamaIndex patterns), proxy/gateway placement in front of Redwood (rate limits, quotas, single-tenant gateway), and options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC). Security emphasis: SAML SSO, KMS, audit logs, and data residency. Next step: send pricing + security docs and run a 2-week pilot benchmark.

Topics: SDK examples, gateway/proxy placement, batching and KV cache, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks (token-level cost & traces), VPC/private deployment, SOC2/KMS, pilot scope.

Action items (captured here for quick scan): see metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey all, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, I'll be the AE on this. With me Priya and Ethan from SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya Patel: Doing well, thanks. Excited to dig in.
[00:15] Daniel Ortiz: Hey. Quick note we might have to jump between network meetings at 4:45 — but we'll stay as long as we can.
[00:18] Jordan: Totally fine. Quick agenda: 1) understand your stack and constraints, 2) talk integration patterns (SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex), 3) discuss gateway/proxy and rate limiting options, 4) security + deployment modes, 5) next steps.
[00:32] Priya Singh: I'll take the integration part, show some examples and ask about your current runtime.
[00:36] Maya: Great. For context, AcornWave runs a consumer chat product plus an internal search index. We're using a mix of microservices on EKS, and a few serverless functions for inference spikes. Our current evals were with OpenAI but the cost profile is high and we want better control/regulatory posture.
[00:50] Priya: Understood. When you say search index, is that embedding-based retrieval with something like LlamaIndex or custom?
[00:56] Tom Alvarez: We're using LlamaIndex for orchestration and FAISS as the vector store. We glue some LangChain chains for prompt management.
[01:04] Ethan Cole: Helpful. So you've got an existing LangChain/LlamaIndex layer which makes SDK integration straightforward. You'd call Redwood via our SDK or directly through a gateway, and keep your retrieval pipeline intact.
[01:15] Daniel: Can you explain the tradeoffs between calling Redwood directly from microservices vs routing through our internal gateway? We have rate limits and per-team quotas already.
[01:24] Priya: Yeah — two main patterns: 1) service direct: each microservice calls Redwood's Hosted API or Dedicated endpoint with keys; good for simplicity and low-hop latency. 2) proxy/gateway path: route requests through your edge gateway where you can enforce per-team quotas, pre/post-processing, tracing, and cache prefixes. That gives you central control but adds a hop and you need to ensure the gateway can handle streaming.
[01:43] Maya: We need streaming for the chat product, and our gateway uses Envoy sidecars. Any caveats?
[01:49] Priya: Envoy is fine — many customers put a reverse-proxy in front. A few details: make sure you handle chunked transfer encoding and streaming timeouts; Redwood supports streaming over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 and we recommend passing through chunked streams end-to-end. Also consider connection pooling to avoid head-of-line issues.
[02:06] Li Wei: From security: we can't have customer PII leave our VPC in plain text without controls. Does Redwood offer Private deployment or VPC peering?
[02:13] Jordan: Yes — three options: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool with network isolation), and Private (VPC/private control plane or on-prem). For regulated PII, many enterprise customers use Dedicated with VPC peering or the Private deployment so keys and traffic stay within customer-managed networking.
[02:29] Li Wei: Does Dedicated guarantee no co-tenancy?
[02:32] Jordan: Dedicated is single-customer capacity — you don't share GPUs with other tenants. Data plane is isolated to your capacity. For strictest isolation, Private deployment puts the control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[02:42] Li Wei: What about KMS integration and HSM?
[02:45] Ethan: We integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and have options for KMS/HSM-backed key storage on Private. For Hosted we use a credentials control and can support customer-managed keys for certain enterprise contracts — we'll include the whitepaper on key management.
[02:59] Daniel: Rate limiting — can we do per-user and per-route quotas? We want to throttle expensive long-form generation separately from cheap embedding ops.
[03:07] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports token-based and request-based quotas. You can set per-route SLOs and per-token budgets. Common pattern: a route for embeddings (lower cost per token) with a higher QPS but lower token budget, and a separate chat route with stricter token caps. You can also attach cost accounting to teams so billing maps to internal owners.
[03:27] Tom: Does the SDK expose usage headers for token counts?
[03:30] Priya: We emit token counts and cost estimates in response headers and via the console. There's also a tracing hook so you can correlate tokens per request with your distributed traces.
[03:38] Maya: How well does Redwood's SDK play with LangChain? We need example code for LlamaIndex + LangChain calling Redwood for embeddings and chat.
[03:45] Priya: We have SDK plugins/snippets for LangChain and LlamaIndex. For embeddings you swap in RedwoodEmbeddings class; for chat you can use the RedwoodChat wrapper which supports streaming callbacks. We'll share a repo with examples where LlamaIndex uses Redwood embeddings and LangChain chains call RedwoodChat.
[03:58] Daniel: Any gotchas with chunked responses and LangChain's callback handlers?
[04:02] Ethan: LangChain's streaming callbacks expect a few events; we've implemented adapters in the example that translate Redwood stream frames into LangChain events. The other thing is to align finish reasons and partial tokens — sometimes ASR style partials can be dropped if not handled.
[04:17] Maya: Curious about batching and KV cache — our prompt patterns reuse context across many requests and we want to minimize token costs.
[04:23] Priya: Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching and we have configurable batching windows. For high reuse you can enable prefix caching which stores repeated prefixes; KV cache helps with multi-turn chat and reduces repeated attention work. We'll discuss quantization and recommend model variants that balance perf and fidelity.
[04:39] Tom: If we run the pilot, can you run a config with 8-bit quantized model vs FP16 so we can measure latency/cost tradeoffs?
[04:45] Priya: Yep, pilot can include multiple model variants. For Dedicated we can pin the quantization profile. For Hosted we may recommend a verified quantized variant; we'll note differences in the benchmark report.
[04:55] Daniel: Observability: we need token-level cost attribution + per-request traces in our existing Jaeger stack. How do we integrate?
[05:02] Ethan: Two options: 1) use the Redwood tracing plugin that emits spans with request_id and token breakdown which you can ship to Jaeger/Zipkin; 2) ingest our JSON cost logs via S3 or a push endpoint into your pipeline. Many customers do both — tracing for low-latency debug and logs for billing reconciliation.
[05:18] Li Wei: Audit logs retention — what's default and can we extend?
[05:22] Jordan: Hosted has configurable retention tiers; enterprise can enable extended retention and immutable audit logs for compliance. Private deployments let you control retention entirely. We'll include our audit log spec and retention SLAs.
[05:33] Maya: On a practical level, what's the onboarding time for going from POC to Dedicated? We have a Q1 2027 target for launch.
[05:39] Jordan: Typical timeline: POC + benchmarking 2–4 weeks, Dedicated provisioned in 2–6 weeks depending on capacity and region, Dedicated SLA and network config might add 1–2 weeks. For Q1 that seems reasonable if we start the pilot this month.
[05:52] Daniel: Cost — we need a baseline estimate. For large scale we care about per-token unit economics plus reserved capacity.
[05:57] Jordan: We'll send a worksheet that models per-token cost for Hosted vs Dedicated committed monthly usage. Dedicated lowers per-token but requires commitment for predictable throughput. There's also model/quantization recommendations that materially change unit cost.
[06:09] Tom: Any limitations on number of API keys or RBAC scopes for teams?
[06:13] Priya: We support fine-grained RBAC, unlimited API keys per account, and you can bind keys to routes and quota buckets. For SSO we support SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[06:24] Li Wei: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for some customer segments.
[06:28] Jordan: We have region controls; Hosted runs in multiple regions and you can pin models to EU regions. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated with region-specific capacity or Private deployment in your region.
[06:39] Maya: We want to run a pilot that exercises: chat streaming at 20rps with 1k token average, embedding pipeline at 200rps, and a background rerank job. Can Redwood simulate that?
[06:49] Priya: Yes, provide sample prompts and traces. We'll run two configs: Hosted baseline and Dedicated with autoscaling disabled to show reserved throughput. We'll measure 50th, 95th, and 99th latencies plus token costs.
[06:59] Daniel: Who from Redwood will own the pilot and be our contact for infra issues?
[07:03] Jordan: Priya will own the technical pilot, I'll coordinate commercial, and Ethan will help on observability integrations.
[07:09] Maya: Ok. On legal + procurement, we'll need a SOC2 attestation, DPA, and a standard CSP appendix.
[07:16] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 and DPA and can loop in legal if anything unusual is needed.
[07:21] Li Wei: One more question: can we run a private deployment in our AWS account (airgapped not fully but VPC only)?
[07:28] Ethan: Yes, Private supports customer-managed VPC and can be deployed into customer AWS accounts; there are network requirements and an installation window typically 4–8 weeks. We'll include the network diagram and ops checklist.
[07:40] Tom: A little nit: do you provide an SDK in Go? Our backend is Go heavy.
[07:44] Priya: We have official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go has an official maintained client; if you need generated client we can provide examples and a Go LangChain adapter.
[07:53] Daniel: Any pre-built Helm charts or operator for Dedicated/private on k8s?
[07:57] Ethan: For Private we provide Helm charts and an operator for lifecycle management; we'll share the repo. For Dedicated we manage infra but can provide certs and kube configs for peering.
[08:08] Maya: Thanks — this was super helpful. Quick recap before we finish?
[08:12] Jordan: Sure — recap: 1) AcornWave will provide prompt set + 1GB sample + expected traffic profiles. 2) Redwood will run benchmark on Hosted and Dedicated quantized variants. 3) Redwood to send pricing worksheet, SOC2/DPA, KMS whitepaper, network diagram. 4) Pilot kickoff week of 2026-11-22. 5) Decision target: early Jan 2027.
[08:34] Maya: That timeline works.
[08:36] Daniel: We'll aim to get artifacts to you by the 18th.
[08:39] Jordan: Great. Anything else?
[08:42] Li Wei: Please include how audit retention and SAML mapping to RBAC works in the security doc.
[08:48] Jordan: Noted.
[08:50] Maya: Appreciate it.
[08:52] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc pack and the pilot proposal.
[08:58] -- Meeting end --
